messages:
raj: quick follow-up to the GQA/MQA kernel RFC — after enabling grouped-query in canary we saw tail latency spikes during short-seq traffic bursts, anyone seen this?

sasha: yup saw it earlier today on eu-west-1 canary. p95 jumped ~120ms -> ~260ms for some routes. looks correlated with many concurrent tiny requests (<= 32 tokens).

mike: interesting. do you have a traffic sample and profiler traces? could be KV cache lock contention or suboptimal kernel path selection.

raj: attaching brief log excerpt (trimmed):
```
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z request_id=abc123 seq_len=18 grouped_query=true device=gpux1 kernel=grouped_attn_v2 latency_ms=243
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z request_id=def456 seq_len=20 grouped_query=true device=gpux1 kernel=grouped_attn_v2 latency_ms=255
2026-03-18T14:12:03Z request_id=ghi789 seq_len=512 grouped_query=false kernel=mqa_attn latency_ms=30
```

sasha: that pattern screams small-batch overhead. grouped_query introduces extra gather/scatter and per-group bookkeeping. When most requests are short, overhead dominates.

anya: can we switch heuristics so grouped-query only triggers when avg_seq_len >= 64 OR batch_size >= 8?

mike: partial yes. Right now kernel selector uses a simple cost model: estimated_ops = seq_len^2 * token_count * kernel_factor. But kernel_factor is static per-kernel and doesn't capture constant overheads.

raj: proposal: add a constant "setup_cost" term per kernel to the cost heuristic:
```json
{"kernel": "grouped_attn_v2", "setup_cost_ms": 0.8, "per_token_cost": 0.002}
{"kernel": "mqa_attn", "setup_cost_ms": 0.05, "per_token_cost": 0.004}
```
selector picks kernel with lower (setup_cost + per_token_cost * effective_tokens).

sasha: that would let us prefer MQA for tiny requests even if asymptotically grouped-query is cheaper. makes sense. we should derive setup_cost from microbenchmarks per-device.

mike: +1. also we should consider contention: shared KV cache access has a lock when groups span allocations; add a multiplier when concurrent_groups > threshold.

anya: sounds more complex to compute at request time. Could we approximate with simple rules: if seq_len < 48 and group_count <=2 then prefer mqa; else grouped.

raj: I want a middle ground: baseline cost model with measured setup_cost, but expose an override flag `force_layout_preference` per-route for immediate rollbacks. Keep the simple rule as a fast-path.

infra-bot: canary deploy 1781239 -> eng-runtime/gqa-mqa-canary-2 started by raj at 2026-03-18T14:20:01Z

sasha: one more thing — quantized kernels (int8/q4) change setup vs per-token tradeoff. Setup_cost for quant kernels is higher due to reordering; need kernel variants keyed by quantization profile.

mike: good catch. we'll model cost by (kernel, quant_profile). Add metrics tags: kernel_hint + quant_profile so we can slice quickly. Sasha, can you add those to console dashboards?

sasha: on it. adding p50/p95/p99, concurrency, avg_seq_len, grouped_query_ratio, kernel_hint.

raj: action items: 1) mike to add setup_cost term and quant_profile key into kernel selector prototype (PR) — target EOD Friday. 2) sasha to add dashboards and microbenchmark harness for per-device setup_cost. 3) anya to add a short RFC addendum describing the cost model and rollback override. 4) i'll run a 10% canary after PR merges.

mike: I'm going to prototype a fallback check: if grouped kernel selected but observed latency > baseline * 2 for first 100 requests then automatically fallback to mqa for that route for 2 minutes. cheap safeguard.

anya: love the auto-fallback idea. reduces blast radius. make it opt-in for now.

raj: agreed opt-in. also need a small API tweak: add `kernel_hint` to the per-route config so product teams can prefer lower-latency kernels for interactive features. we'll document it.

infra-bot: canary 1781239 report: 10% traffic, matched rules, initial p95 delta +110ms on small routes.

mike: OK that's the observed delta. once setup_cost model in place we should see this reduce.

anya: timeline? mike EOD PR, sasha dashboards tomorrow, raj canary next Tuesday?

raj: timeline works. mike — ping here when PR is up. I'll schedule canary after CI passes.

mike: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2145 — adds setup_cost and quant_profile keys. comments welcome.

sasha: ack, wiring dashboards now.

anya: I'll draft RFC addendum and link to PR.

raj: sounds good. thanks all. small ask — keep the messages short in the RFC addendum, plus a simple diagram showing selector flow.

mike: will do.

sasha: +1 :thumbsup:

anya: :rocket:

raj: closing thread — follow-ups tracked in the RFC board.
